summary: On node1, built a persistent LVM-backed filesystem for /srv/data (loop-attached backing file → LVM PV/VG/LV → XFS, mounted via fstab, loop attachment made boot-persistent via a systemd unit ordered before LVM activation). Populated /srv/data with application data, took an LVM COW snapshot (data_snap), then modified the live directory (deleted files, tampered config, added a rogue file). Restored the directory to the exact pre-modification state via `lvconvert --merge` and verified byte-for-byte via sha256 manifest diff (zero differences). Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id + health baseline, rebooted via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed boot_id changed, and confirmed the loop device, LVM VG/LV, mount, and data content all recovered automatically and matched the baseline exactly.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 disk/filesystem layout (single XFS root partition, no LVM/Btrfs, no spare disk)
Created a 3G loopback backing file and a systemd unit (srv-data-loop.service) to attach it at /dev/loop20 before LVM activation, enabled at boot
Created LVM PV/VG (srv_data_vg)/LV (data, 2G), formatted XFS, added persistent /etc/fstab entry, mounted at /srv/data
Populated /srv/data with application config and 20 record files; captured a sha256 baseline manifest
Created LVM COW snapshot data_snap (700M) capturing that state
Modified /srv/data: deleted 2 files, tampered config, added a rogue file, altered another file; diffed against baseline to confirm the change was real
Restored via `lvconvert --merge` on the snapshot, reactivated the VG/LV, remounted, and verified sha256 manifest matches baseline exactly (no diff)
Captured pre-restart boot_id, uptime, mount/LVM health, and data-integrity baseline
Issued `systemctl reboot` on node1 with an ack that returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again; confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset
Verified post-reboot: loop device reattached, VG/LV active, /srv/data mounted, and data sha256 manifest still matches the original baseline exactly

evidence.requirement: Filesystem snapshot mechanism established and application data populated under /srv/data
evidence.summary: Confirmed no existing LVM/Btrfs, then built LVM PV/VG/LV on a boot-persistent loopback device, mounted XFS at /srv/data, populated it with application data, and captured a sha256 baseline manifest.

evidence.requirement: Snapshot captured before modification, directory modified, then restored to exact snapshot content
evidence.summary: Took LVM snapshot data_snap, modified /srv/data (deleted files, tampered config, added rogue file) with diff proving the change, then ran lvconvert --merge to roll back and diffed the resulting sha256 manifest against baseline showing zero differences ('RESTORE VERIFIED: content matches baseline exactly').

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state for node1
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (cce73776...), mount/LVM/data health baseline; issued systemctl reboot; confirmed boot_id changed to 182fdfdf... with new uptime; confirmed post-reboot loop device, LVM VG/LV, /srv/data mount, and data sha256 manifest all recovered and matched baseline exactly.
